_comment: gBrain / Hermes multi-LLM failover chain. Providers are tried in ascending priority order. The wrapper (llm_router.py) reads this file. Model IDs and API keys are the ONLY things you normally edit.

router._fail_open_note: If true, a request that exhausts every provider returns an error object instead of raising. Keep false so Hermes can decide what to do.

failover._comment: Conditions that make the router ABANDON the current provider and move to the next one. A non-matching error (e.g. a malformed prompt / 400 bad_request) is treated as fatal and is NOT failed over, because the next provider would fail identically.

retry_same_provider._comment: Transient errors (429/5xx) are retried on the SAME provider before failing over, honoring any Retry-After header. Hard quota/billing errors skip straight to the next provider.

providers.name: openai
providers.label: OpenAI Codex (primary)
providers._model_note: Set to the exact model your linked Codex/OpenAI account serves (e.g. gpt-5.1, gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-4.1). This is the model string, not the product name.

providers.name: anthropic
providers.label: Claude (secondary / backup)
providers._model_note: claude-opus-4-8 is the current Opus. Use claude-sonnet-5 for cheaper high-volume fallback if desired.
providers._thinking_note: Set adaptive_thinking true to let Claude reason on hard prompts (adds latency/cost). Leave false for drop-in parity with the other providers.

providers.name: gemini
providers.label: Gemini (tertiary / final fallback)
providers._model_note: Set to the exact Gemini model your key can access (e.g. gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash).
